transcript_claim: The Merck-Moderna Phase 3 melanoma trial succeeded on its primary endpoints.
notes: The trial met both RFS and DMFS; OS remains immature.

transcript_claim: The vaccine reduced recurrence or death by 42%.
evidence: HR 0.58 corresponds to a 42% relative reduction in the hazard of recurrence or death.
notes: Relative, not absolute, risk reduction.

transcript_claim: At two years, 82% of vaccinated patients were recurrence-free versus 70% of controls.
notes: Absolute difference is 12.2 percentage points; NNT approximately 8.2.

transcript_claim: The benefit appears only after the six-month immunization period.
evidence: First 6 months RFS HR 0.99 (0.66-1.49); after 6 months piecewise RFS HR 0.42 (0.30-0.58).
notes: Pre-specified sensitivity analysis; first-six-month DMFS HR 1.01 (0.58-1.79).

transcript_claim: The trial proved that the vaccine extends overall survival.
evidence: OS HR 0.77 (0.45-1.31), p=.33; OS data immature.
notes: A favorable trend is not statistically significant evidence of survival benefit.

transcript_claim: The Phase 3 effect is similar to the Phase 2 result.
evidence: Phase 2 5-year RFS reduction 49% (HR 0.51); Phase 3 42% (HR 0.58).
notes: Directionally consistent but attenuated by 7 percentage points.

transcript_claim: The distant-metastasis benefit replicated at full strength.
evidence: Phase 2 DMFS reduction 59% (HR 0.41); Phase 3 38% (HR 0.62).
notes: Attenuation is larger for DMFS than for RFS, consistent with winner's curse.

transcript_claim: The trial enrolled about 1,100 patients.
evidence: 1,137 randomized 2:1 (757 combination, 380 control).
notes: Registry still lists 1,089 as estimated enrollment; the registry is stale.

transcript_claim: The melanoma vaccine is already approved and available.
evidence: Companies are engaging regulators; the only Moderna mRNA vaccine approved is MFLUSIVA for influenza.
notes: No FDA approval for intismeran in melanoma was found.

transcript_claim: The vaccine has been shown to work across cancers.
evidence: The pivotal evidence is in resected stage IIB-IV melanoma; other tumors are still under study.
notes: One positive melanoma trial does not establish pan-cancer efficacy.

transcript_claim: The October data leak showed negative results.
evidence: CNBC reports a partial leak followed by full positive data; the 42% RFS reduction was clinically meaningful.
notes: The leak created a disclosure shock, not a negative efficacy result.

transcript_claim: Moderna fell 25% because the data were bad.
evidence: Intraday decline reached about 25%; close was -17.57%. Full data were positive.
notes: The direction of the drop is supported; the causal claim is not. Analysts attributed it to inflated expectations.

transcript_claim: Moderna fell from above $100 to below $10.
evidence: Closing trough after the 2021 peak was $22.36 on 2025-11-20.
notes: The stock fell about 95% from its peak but never closed below $10.

transcript_claim: Moderna lost two-thirds of its value in 2023.
evidence: 2023 total return was -44.63%.
notes: The two-thirds-scale decline belongs to 2024 (-58.19%), not 2023.

transcript_claim: Moderna's sales collapsed to $3 billion in 2023.
evidence: 2023 total revenue was $6.848B; 2024 total revenue was $3.236B.
notes: The $3B-scale collapse occurred in 2024, one year later.

transcript_claim: Moderna's market capitalization exceeded $200 billion.
evidence: Peak intraday $497.42 x 403.6M shares ≈ $200.8B; peak close $484.47 x 403.6M ≈ $195.6B.
notes: A >$200B valuation is reproducible only on an intraday peak using contemporaneous shares; the closing peak was below $200B.

transcript_claim: Moderna made about $18 billion in 2021 and $36 billion across its first two commercial years.
evidence: 2021 total revenue $18.471B; 2021-2022 total revenue $37.734B; product sales $36.110B.
notes: The $36B figure is product sales; total revenue was $37.7B.

transcript_claim: Moderna has about 4,500 employees.
evidence: 10-K reports approximately 4,700 full-time employees as of 2025-12-31.
notes: Order of magnitude is right; the exact figure is outdated by roughly 200.

transcript_claim: Moderna designed its COVID vaccine and dosed the first human within 63 days.
evidence: Company timeline: 63 days from sequence selection to first Phase 1 dose; NIH says 65 days from sequence release.
notes: Both are defensible depending on whether the clock starts at sequence release or selection.

transcript_claim: HHS canceled 22 mRNA projects worth $500 million.
evidence: HHS says the wind-down affects 22 projects worth nearly $500 million.
notes: The precise wording is 'nearly $500 million'; separate Moderna bird-flu cancellation is part of the same wind-down.

transcript_claim: HHS concluded that mRNA vaccines fail to protect against respiratory infections.
evidence: HHS Secretary quote: 'the data show these vaccines fail to protect effectively against upper respiratory infections like COVID and flu.'
notes: This grades the existence of the claim, not its scientific correctness; the statement is contested by clinical evidence.

transcript_claim: The FDA approved Moderna's mRNA flu vaccine.
evidence: MFLUSIVA approved August 5, 2026 for adults 50 and older.
notes: Traditional approval 50-64; accelerated approval 65+ based on immunogenicity.

transcript_claim: Moderna's flu vaccine is 27% stronger than the standard flu vaccine.
evidence: Relative vaccine efficacy 26.6% (95% CI 16.7-35.4) vs standard-dose comparator; 27.4% in adults 65+.
notes: Relative, not absolute, efficacy; the comparator was a standard-dose vaccine, not no vaccine.

transcript_claim: The flu approval proves the cancer vaccine works.
evidence: MFLUSIVA and intismeran are different products with different endpoints and mechanisms of action.
notes: Platform-level inference is not product-level evidence.

transcript_claim: Merck paid $200 million in 2016 and $250 million in 2022 for the mRNA cancer vaccine partnership.
evidence: 2016 upfront $200M; 2022 option exercise $250M; costs and profits shared equally.
notes: The 2022 payment was an option exercise, not a new upfront partnership.

transcript_claim: Keytruda is about one-third of Merck's revenue.
evidence: 2022 Keytruda sales $20.937B of $59.283B total, or 35.3%.
notes: This is a 2022 snapshot; the share is higher in later years.

transcript_claim: Keytruda's patent expires in 2028.
evidence: 10-K: compound patent expires December 2028; two additional patents expire May and November 2029.
notes: Merck plans conservatively for 2028 loss of exclusivity.

transcript_claim: Merck owns the cancer vaccine.
evidence: Merck exercised an option to jointly develop and commercialize; costs and profits are shared 50/50.
notes: Joint ownership/economic partnership, not sole ownership.

transcript_claim: Each personalized vaccine takes about six weeks to manufacture.
evidence: CNBC reports the personalized manufacturing process can take six weeks.
notes: Company says the timeline may shorten; this is a current-process estimate.

transcript_claim: Moderna's stock rose roughly fivefold in 2026.
notes: As of 2026-10-23 the YTD return was +578.5%.

transcript_claim: Short sellers lost $5.5 billion on Moderna's August surge.
evidence: Reported by Bloomberg/S3 as a $5.5B paper loss; the underlying short-interest data are proprietary.
notes: The number is widely reported but not independently reproducible from public data.

transcript_claim: Moderna was worth about $25 billion before the Phase 3 topline.
evidence: 62.96 close times 399,235,889 shares equals $25.14B.
notes: Close-to-close basis on 2026-08-18.

transcript_claim: Moderna added about $44 billion in market value on the topline day.
evidence: Close-to-close change from $25.14B to $69.62B, or +$44.48B.
notes: Reuters cited about $30B intraday; the difference is timing.

transcript_claim: The vaccine prevents melanoma.
evidence: It is an adjuvant treatment after complete resection of stage IIB-IV melanoma; it reduces recurrence and distant metastasis.
notes: Not a primary preventive vaccine for healthy people.

transcript_claim: The absolute benefit is about 12 percentage points at two years.
evidence: 82.2% minus 70.0% equals 12.2 percentage points.
notes: Corresponds to roughly 8.2 patients treated per additional recurrence-free patient.

transcript_claim: The Phase 3 results are peer-reviewed and published.
evidence: Accepted for publication in the New England Journal of Medicine; presented at ESMO 2026 as LBA1.
notes: Accepted is not the same as published; no DOI was found as of 2026-10-24.

transcript_claim: The FDA approved Moderna's melanoma cancer vaccine.
evidence: No melanoma approval was found; companies are engaging regulators after Phase 3.
notes: Do not confuse the 2026 influenza approval with an oncology approval.

transcript_claim: The October drop was a one-day 25% collapse.
evidence: Intraday high-to-low was -25.06%; close-to-close was -17.57%.
notes: The 25% figure is an intraday range, not the closing return.

transcript_claim: The 2023 crash was the whole de-rating.
evidence: Annual returns: 2023 -44.63%, 2024 -58.19%, 2025 -29.08%; trough in November 2025.
notes: The decline was multi-year, not a single 2023 event.

transcript_claim: The vaccine's benefit is larger than the trial's overall hazard ratio suggests.
evidence: Overall RFS HR 0.58; post-six-month piecewise HR 0.42.
notes: The overall average dilutes the delayed treatment effect.

transcript_claim: Merck also fell sharply when the positive data were released.
notes: Two different events; the large positive move was on the topline.

transcript_claim: The stock reaction is evidence that the data were negative.
evidence: The data were positive; the selloff followed a partial leak and elevated expectations.
notes: Price reaction is not an efficacy endpoint.
